newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-MCGRATH LEADS AUSTRALIAN COUNTER-ATTACK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MCGRATH LEADS AUSTRALIAN COUNTER-ATTACK.

text.p: Australian fast bowler Glenn McGrath seized three quick wickets to throw the third and final cricket test against South Africa back into the melting pot at Centurion Park on Sunday.

South Africa slumped from their overnight 240 for three to be 298 for seven at lunch as four wickets fell for just 58 runs in the morning session. That gave the home side a 71-run lead over Australia who were bowled out for 227 in their first innings.
McGrath bowled 14 unchanged overs in the session in a spell of three for 23 to give him match figures of five for 67 and his sixth five-wicket haul in 28 tests.
His victims included opener Adam Bacher who laboured for 84 minutes in scoring just two runs before he was out six short of a maiden test century.
Jason Gillespie removed nightwatchman Pat Symcox in the sixth over of the day when the batsman miscued to mid-off.

Jacques Kallis spliced a rising delivery from McGrath to Steve Waugh diving forward in the gully -- refusing to walk until the square leg umpire confirmed the catch had been made cleanly -- as South Africa stumbled to 255 for five.
And in the space of three balls in his 10th over of the day McGrath had made it 262 for seven.
Bacher was trapped leg before wicket as he tried to work a straight ball through square leg and Dave Richardson gloved a bouncer onto his stumps.
Bacher had batted seven and a half hours and faced 322 balls when he was finally out, striking 10 fours and a six.
Hansie Cronje (22 not out) and Lance Klusener (19 not out) took South Africa through to lunch without further mishap with a 36-run partnership.
